ledger.claim: POL-NS-09(c) is a mandatory escalation trigger on this record. rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 2 and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 2, so two or more no-show disputes between this same rider and this same driver fall inside the trailing 90 days — which is exactly what the rider means when the claim says this is 'another dispute with the same driver'. A single trip's record cannot fairly resolve a repeat pairwise conflict in either direction, so the case must go to a human reviewer rather than be closed by the automated pipeline.

Escalation under POL-NS-09 is terminal and, per POL-GEN-03, replaces any monetary ruling: the disputed amount is held rather than collected or refunded, and the rider's claim is not disposed of against the rider while review is pending. The fare breakdown shows the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee sitting at payment_status PENDING, charged_at null and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so an escalated file leaves the rider carrying no charge at all.

The in-app log shows the rider engaging on the pickup during the waiting window — 'Coming down now' sent at 06:51:40, answered by the driver's 'Okay, waiting' at 06:52:00 — and the driver cancelling three and a half minutes later at 06:55:30. That is a live coordination conflict between a repeat rider-driver pair, which is precisely the pattern POL-NS-09(c) reserves for human review instead of an automated single-case disposition.

EV-ADVIS-09110-01 is MISSING — issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, BLOCKING severity, weight_multiplier 0.0 — so no traffic advisory exists for this pickup road or waiting window. The driver therefore cannot credit any advisory-permitted accumulation under POL-NS-06(i): the in-geofence dwell stands on the trace alone, and no lawful-obstruction argument can be built on an artifact that carries no payload. I disclose the impairment and its issue code as POL-GEN-02 requires.

The driver's own GPS trace places him inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius for the whole waiting window: all 34 driver fixes sit roughly 24 m from the pickup pin (min 24.01 m, max 24.01 m) at a constant 0.0 km/h, and all 34 pass the 25 m accuracy filter as qualifying in-radius fixes, so POL-NS-02 is satisfied and POL-NS-01 limb (b) is met. Because he was inside the radius rather than outside it, the wrong-entrance route in POL-NS-03 is not engaged at all.

The dwell is a single continuous in-geofence hold of 330 seconds, running from the first qualifying fix at 06:50:00 to the last at 06:55:30 — 30 seconds more than the 300-second minimum for a STANDARD pickup — so POL-NS-01 limb (c) is carried, and the record shows a -30.0 second shortfall basis, i.e. a surplus, not a shortfall.

The trip record carries the driver 'arrived' event at 06:50:20 and terminates the trip driver-side at 06:55:30 with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, after the required dwell had elapsed, with no boarding event recorded — POL-NS-01 limbs (a) and (d) are both satisfied.

There is no false arrival marker under POL-NS-05: at the 06:50:20 arrival event the trace puts the driver about 24 m from the pin and stationary at 0.0 km/h, nowhere near the 300 m distance trigger or the 15 km/h speed trigger, and the in-geofence fix at 06:50:00 actually precedes the marker, so the arrival timestamp is honest rather than premature.

The rider-exonerating clause POL-NS-04 cannot run on this record: the driver answered the rider's 06:51:40 message 'Coming down now.' with 'Okay, waiting.' at 06:52:00 — 20 seconds later, well inside the 120 second window — and he had already posted 'At Block 612 lobby pickup.' at 06:50:35, so limb (b) fails and the clause does not apply.

Independently, the rider's own device was never at the pickup point: all 16 rider fixes sit about 519 m from the pin, more than five times the 100 m STANDARD rider presence radius, and 0 rider fixes qualify, so POL-NS-04 limb (c) is affirmatively failed on admissible fixes and any residual issue falls back to POL-NS-01.

With POL-NS-01 carried in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displacing it, POL-NS-07 pays the driver 80 percent of the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee itemised in the ledger — SGD 3.20 — and the anti-farming guard is not tripped: 1 no-show termination in 30 days is below the threshold of 4, and 1/120 completed trips is 0.008, below 0.08.

The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-09110-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — I disclose that impairment and do not rest on it. It is irrelevant here because the 330 second hold is one unbroken in-geofence run, so no accumulation of separate intervals under POL-NS-06(i) is needed to reach the minimum.

Only the citable trailing-window counter bears on POL-NS-07: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1, and the lifetime prior_no_show_flags figure of 2 is context only — POL-GEN-01 forbids reading the lifetime counter in place of the 30 day one, so no adverse pattern can be built against this driver.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this dispute goes to a human reviewer and no money moves. The SGD 4.00 cancellation fee is placed on hold — it is not collected from the rider and not refunded to them while review is pending.

On the merits, the driver's account is well supported. The trip record carries an 'arrived' event at 06:50:20 and shows the driver terminating the trip at 06:55:30 with reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW and no boarding event, and the GPS trace places his vehicle about 24 m from the pickup pin — inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius — stationary at 0 km/h for one continuous in-geofence hold running 06:50:00 to 06:55:30, i.e. 330 seconds against a 300-second minimum. POL-NS-01 limbs (a) to (d) are therefore all met. There is no false arrival marker (POL-NS-05: he was ~24 m out and stopped, far from the 300 m/15 km/h triggers), and no waiting-period shortfall (POL-NS-06), so nothing displaces the charge. The rider's device sat about 519 m from the pin, so POL-NS-04 does not assist them either. Left there, POL-NS-07 would pay the driver SGD 3.20 (80% of SGD 4.00), and the anti-farming guard is not tripped (1 no-show termination in 30 days, and 1/120 = 0.008 of completed trips, both below the thresholds).

That outcome cannot be issued, however. POL-NS-09(c) makes escalation mandatory where rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d together show 2 or more no-show disputes between the same rider and driver in the trailing 90 days. Both records show 2, and the rider's own claim describes this as 'another dispute with the same driver'. Escalation under POL-NS-09 is terminal and, per POL-GEN-03, replaces any monetary ruling — so the driver's compensation claim is accepted in substance but not paid out by the automated pipeline, and the rider's request is neither granted nor denied here.

The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-09110-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) and carries no fact; it decides nothing, because the 330-second hold is a single unbroken interval and no accumulation under POL-NS-06(i) was needed.

Question for the reviewer: whether this pair's repeated no-show disputes reflect a recurring genuine pickup problem or possible abuse on either side — a question a single trip's record cannot fairly settle.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
